title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X is a real surface (a 2‑manifold with a differentiable structure at x, at least C^1), x is a point of X, and D_x^* is the punctured germ of disc at x. The previous page reduces the goal to building a functor (87) A_x → Revêt(D_x^*). Here A_x is the category of closed arcs on the circle of tangent directions at x, ordered by inclusion; the page writes A_n, apparently for A_x. The functor is read as giving, for each arc, a 'fibre functor' (a base point) on the category of coverings of D_x^*. The criterion (86/86bis) is that the groupoid obtained by inverting all inclusions of arcs maps equivalently onto the fundamental groupoid of D_x^*. That holds if the target is connected, has π_1 ≅ Z, and the loop {a}→A←{b}→B←{a} (A, B the two arcs between distinct points a, b) goes to a generator.

To build (87) it suffices to give (88): a functor from arcs to contractible ('1‑connected') germs of spaces over the germ D_x^*. Line (89) states the general principle that such germs define fibre functors on Revêt(D_x^*): take sections, or the fibre over a simply connected germ.

Construction on this page:
- Each arc A corresponds to a closed cone C in the tangent plane Tang_x(X), other than {0} and the whole plane. Let CA_x be the set of these cones.
- Choose a local isomorphism f:(Tang_x X,0) ≅ (X,x) with tangent map the identity (90).
- The image f(C) depends on f. Instead take the filter base of all cones C' in CA_x strictly containing C, meaning C'−{0} is a neighbourhood of C−{0}.
- Next page: the filter on X−{x} generated by f(V ∩ (C'−{0})), with V running over neighbourhoods of 0, does not depend on f and tends to x.
- This filter gives a germ of space C̃ over D_x^*. It is contractible, because each V ∩ (C'−{0}) with V convex is a punctured star‑shaped sector, homotopy equivalent to an arc.
- Inclusions A1 ⊂ A2 give maps C̃1 → C̃2. This yields (88), hence (87), and the equivalence of groupoids is checked through (86bis).

In modern terms this is a chart‑independent, purely topological/differential construction of tangential (sectorial) base points at a puncture. It presents the fundamental groupoid of the punctured disc through the groupoid of sectors with inclusions inverted.
errors: Independence from f needs f to be at least C^1 with tangent map the identity, so that angular distortion tends to 0 at x. The strict enlargement C' ⊃⊃ C exactly absorbs this distortion, so the claim is right; Grothendieck states it as evident without proof.

The remark 'take V convex closed, so V∩(C'−{0}) is contractile' is fine as long as C' is not the whole plane. For arcs longer than a half‑circle C' is not convex, but V∩C' is still star‑shaped about 0, and removing 0 leaves something homotopic to an arc. No real gap.

ideas.what: Base points at a puncture given by arcs of tangent directions (sectors), realised as filters/germs of spaces on X−{x} tending to x and independent of the chart, via strictly larger cones
ideas.modern_name: tangential base points (topological version) / sectorial base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, 'Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points', §15); sectors in Stokes theory (Malgrange, Deligne)
ideas.where_published: Base points at infinity are discussed in La Longue Marche (1981) and the Esquisse (1984); this precise filter construction is, as far as I know, not in published texts

ideas.what: The groupoid of arcs of the circle of directions, with inclusions inverted, is equivalent to the fundamental groupoid of the punctured disc (criterion: connected, π1 ≅ Z, the loop through two complementary arcs maps to a generator)
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial/'discrete' model of π1(S^1) by a groupoid of a cover by intervals (van Kampen for a cover by arcs)

ideas.what: Germs of contractible spaces over a punctured germ define fibre functors on its category of coverings
ideas.modern_name: fibre functors from pro‑points / germs at ends
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; related to shape theory and to 'ends'

missed.claim: In unpublished material probably close to 1981, Grothendieck gives a careful topological, chart‑independent definition of tangential base points at punctures of a surface. Base points are sectors or arcs of directions; independence from the chart comes from the filter of strictly larger cones under any local isomorphism whose tangent map is the identity. This predates Deligne's 1989 algebraic definition of tangential base points.
missed.quote: Mais considérons la base de filtre des cônes C' ∈ CA_x contenant strictement C ... (i.e. ... tels que C' − {0} soit un voisinage de C ∖ {0})
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical credit: it documents Grothendieck's own technique for base points at infinity used in the Teichmüller‑tower and Galois action programme. It also offers a clean topological counterpart of tangential base points, useful for comparison isomorphisms. The mathematics itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The construction is elementary and correct. Its interest is mainly historical: an explicit, careful definition of topological tangential (sectorial) base points in Grothendieck's unpublished Longue Marche sequel, before Deligne's standard reference. A specialist would not be surprised by the mathematics.
transcription_corrections: Throughout, 'A_x', 'D_x^*' and 'CA_x' are indexed by x; the previous page's 'A_n' and 'S_n' are likely also x.
'En fait, (88) se résume à : ∀ A ∈ A_x, [un] filtre sur X−x tendant vers x, dit ...' (the insertion 'filtre sur X−x tendant vers x' replaces a struck 'germe ... de X en x').
'Les éléments A de A_x s'identifient évidemment aux cônes fermés C dans Tang_x(X), distincts de {0} et de l'espace tout entier.' The interlinear 'tangent' is part of 'Tang_x(X)'.
(90): 'f : (Tang_x(X), 0) ≃ (X, x), dont l'appl. tangente soit l'identité'.
'son image par un tel isom. dépend du choix de l'iso. local choisi. Mais considérons la base de filtre des cônes C' ∈ CA_x contenant strictement C'.
'Soit CA_x l'ens. de ces cônes' (the transcription has this; the struck 'Si C ...' precedes 'Considérons').
(89) reads: 'cat. des germes d'espaces au-dessus du germe D_x^* → Revêt(D_x^*)'.
